A before and after, straight from the guide

Before

“Write an announcement about the office move.”

After

“Write an announcement for our staff that we’re moving offices on 3 March. Some people are worried about the commute, so keep the tone warm and calm. Make it an email with a subject line, under 150 words. Include the new address and say that parking details will follow next week. Don’t make any promises about desk assignments, because those aren’t decided yet.”

You ask AI for something, and what comes back is too long, too stiff or beside the point. So you correct it, and correct it again. Free plans cap how much you can send, so every correction costs you.

This guide gives you twelve habits for getting a usable answer with less back-and-forth.

It is for people on the free or basic plans of everyday chat apps who aren’t sure AI is worth their time yet. It is also for anyone who has been asked to use more AI at work. You don’t need a paid plan, and you don’t need to code.

A taste of the twelve

  • Give each job its own chat.
  • Paste the real thing instead of describing it.
  • Two strikes, then start fresh.
  • Check its work before your name goes on it.

A sample page

Every commandment has five parts

  • The rule in one line.
  • Why it works, in plain words.
  • A before-and-after example from work and from home.
  • Where to find the setting in your app.
  • A short test to run before you hit send.

Also inside

  • Three kinds of request: plan, make and check. The guide shows you how to keep them apart.
  • Two fill-in sheets you can copy and paste, so the AI knows who you are and writes in your voice.
  • A one-page card with all twelve, to print or keep by your screen.

Three free companion guides

  • Decoded Goes deeper into how to word a request, including giving the AI a role and breaking big jobs into steps.
  • Feed It Your World Shows how to give the AI your own material so its answers fit your situation.
  • What Not to Put Into AI Covers what should never go into an AI chat, such as private, client or company information.
